title: Boho fringed wrap
subtitle: A chunky treble rectangle with a long knotted fringe along both short ends
excerpt: This wrap is a rectangle of treble crochet in chunky-weight yarn on a 6 mm hook, finished with a long knotted fringe along both short ends. The body is entirely plain treble. The fringe is cut, folded through the edge stitches, and knotted at two levels to create a layered macrame-style fringe. Finished size is approximately 180 cm wide by 65 cm deep.
heroPrompt: A boho-style crochet wrap in warm terracotta chunky yarn with a long knotted fringe at each end, draped loosely over a wooden bench, photographed in warm outdoor light.

glossaryTerms.definition: A fringe made by looping cut lengths of yarn through edge stitches and knotting them at two levels: first a simple overhand knot at the root, then the strands from adjacent bundles are split and re-knotted together lower down, creating a net-like macrame pattern.

content.text: This wrap is a straightforward rectangle of treble crochet in chunky yarn on a 6 mm hook. The interest comes from the finishing: a long
knotted fringe
runs along both short ends, knotted twice to create a layered macrame-style cascade. At 180 cm wide by 65 cm deep the wrap covers the shoulders fully and has enough body to drape without slipping.

The crochet body takes less time than the fringe does; plan for the fringe to take as long again as the body. Each fringe bundle uses six strands of yarn cut to 40 cm (they fold to 20 cm plus knot), and there are approximately 80 bundles across both ends combined.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 600 g chunky-weight yarn (body) plus an extra 150 g for fringe. A 6 mm crochet hook (US J/10). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Tape measure. A crochet hook or latch hook for pulling fringe loops through edge stitches.

content.text: Gauge

12 tr x 7 rows = 10 x 10 cm in chunky-weight yarn with a 6 mm hook, measured unstretched. Work a 15 x 15 cm swatch and adjust hook size if needed. Each extra stitch per 10 cm shifts the finished width by about 15 cm.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
treble (tr): UK; the same move as US "double crochet" (dc).
Pattern
The wrap is worked flat from one short end to the other. The foundation chain is the 65 cm depth; the rows build the 180 cm width.
Foundation chain
Ch 79. (This gives 78 working stitches across the 65 cm depth.)
Row 1 (right side)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr throughout). 1 tr in each ch across. Turn. (78 sts)
Rows 2 onwards
Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 1 tr in each st across to end. Turn. (78 sts each row)
Continue to approximately row 126
Continue until the piece measures 180 cm from the foundation chain edge, approximately 126 rows at 7 rows per 10 cm. Fasten off.
Finishing
Fasten off and weave in the two body ends. The fringe is added after.
Cutting fringe strands

Cut lengths of yarn 40 cm long. You need 6 strands per bundle, and approximately 40 bundles along each short end (80 total). Wind the yarn around a 20 cm piece of card and cut along one edge to produce consistent lengths.
Attaching fringe bundles

Hold 6 strands together, fold in half to make a loop of 12 strands doubled. Insert the hook from back to front through the first edge stitch of one short end. Pull the folded loop through. Pass the loose ends through the loop and pull firmly to make a lark's head knot. Repeat in every other stitch (every 2 sts) across the short end. Repeat on the other short end.
First knot row
Working 4 cm below the lark's head knots, gather all 12 strands of each bundle and tie a firm overhand knot. This is the first knot row.
Second knot row

Working 4 cm below the first knot row, split each bundle in half (6 strands each half). Take the right half of one bundle and the left half of the adjacent bundle, combine them, and tie an overhand knot 4 cm below the first knot row. Repeat across all bundles. Leave the outermost half-bundles at each selvedge end un-knotted in this row, or knot them to themselves.
Trim fringe
Once both knot rows are complete on both ends, trim the fringe ends to a straight line with sharp scissors, leaving at least 3 cm of tail below the second knot.
Care
Handwash gently in cool water. Do not tumble-dry or wring. Lay flat to dry and comb the fringe smooth while damp. Fringe can tangle in a washing machine; handwash only.
What to try next

Add a third knot row for a deeper macrame fringe. Work the fringe in a contrast colour for a two-tone effect. A simple chevron pattern in the body (adding and subtracting stitches at regular intervals) works equally well at chunky weight and gives the wrap more visual interest before the fringe is attached.
